sections.h2: PSC oil fell faster than ONGC's nomination oil over the decade

chart.title: Both operator regimes declined, and PSC oil fell by 42%
chart.sub: Crude oil production by regime, MMT: ONGC on nomination, and private operators under production-sharing contracts (PSC). Each point is the fiscal year starting in the year shown.

sections.means: PSC oil fell from 11.78 to 6.79 MMT, a loss of 42%, while ONGC's nomination fields fell by a smaller share.
sections.todo: Read the operator columns separately rather than the national total when judging the decline.

sections.h2: Production targets were missed in every category in FY2024-25

chart.title: Every category missed its FY2024-25 target, by 6–13%
chart.sub: Actual production as a share of target, %.

sections.means: Each category achieved between 87.0% and 93.9% of its target, so the targets work as aspirations rather than forecasts.
sections.todo: Check any production projection against the achievement column, not the target column.

sections.h2: Mumbai Offshore supplies 43.45% of India's crude, so supply rests on one basin

chart.title: Three basins supply 78% of crude, and Mumbai Offshore alone 43.45%
chart.sub: Share of FY2024-25 national crude production, %.

sections.means: Mumbai Offshore alone supplies 43.45% of national crude, so the national total depends heavily on one basin.
sections.todo: Plan replacement supply against the 43.45% share this basin provides, not against incremental drilling elsewhere.
